title: Implement pure technical indicators RSI EMA ATR VWAP and volume
description:
Implement pure, reusable technical indicator functions and incremental calculators in mike_trade/strategies/indicators/core.py, with unit tests in tests/unit/test_indicators.py.

Required behavior:
- All inputs and outputs are Decimal. Use one explicit, documented Decimal context and precision, so results are bit-for-bit reproducible. Do no provider, network, clock, or broker I/O, and keep no global mutable state.
- EMA(period): seed with the SMA of the first `period` values, then apply alpha = 2/(period+1). Return None (or an explicit NotReady marker) until `period` values are available.
- RSI(period): use Wilder smoothing. The first average gain and loss is the simple mean over `period` changes, so `period + 1` closes are needed before the first value. Document and pin the edge cases deterministically: average loss zero with gain > 0 gives 100; both averages zero gives a documented neutral value. The output range is [0, 100].
- ATR(period): true range = max(high - low, |high - prev_close|, |low - prev_close|). The first bar uses high - low. Seed with the simple mean of the first `period` true ranges, then apply Wilder smoothing.
- Session VWAP: cumulative sum(typical_price * volume) / sum(volume), where typical price is (H+L+C)/3. Reset when the session identifier changes; the caller passes it per bar. VWAP is undefined (None) until cumulative session volume > 0. Zero-volume bars do not change VWAP.
- Volume helpers: cumulative session volume (resets with the session id), a simple moving average of volume, and relative volume (current / SMA). Relative volume is None during warmup or when the SMA is zero.
- Provide both batch functions (over a sequence) and incremental stateful calculators. A test must show they produce identical outputs on the same input.
- Each calculator reports its required warmup length (for example `warmup_bars`) and whether it is ready.
- Calculators accept candle-like inputs through a minimal protocol (open/high/low/close/volume, plus a session id for VWAP). Do not import mike_trade/market_data/candles.py, which is built concurrently in h.1.
- Do not encode any trading thresholds or claim profitability.

Before editing, inspect:
- mike_trade/strategies/base.py and mike_trade/domain/strategy_types.py (if present) for existing indicator declaration types or names to align with
- mike_trade/domain/market.py (if present) for bar field names
acceptance_criteria: A test confirms that EMA returns not-ready for the first period-1 inputs, and that the first value equals the SMA seed exactly, using a hand-computed Decimal fixture.

A test confirms that RSI is not ready with exactly `period` closes and ready with `period + 1`. Separate tests pin the all-gains (100) and flat-series (documented neutral) edge cases to exact Decimal values.
A test confirms that ATR uses the gap-inclusive true range (|high - prev_close| dominating) and matches a hand-computed fixture exactly.
A test confirms that session VWAP resets when the session id changes, returns None before any positive volume, and is unaffected by a zero-volume bar.
A test confirms that relative volume is None during warmup and when the volume SMA is zero.
A test confirms that batch and incremental outputs are identical for RSI, EMA, ATR, and VWAP on the same fixture.
A test confirms that every returned numeric value is a Decimal instance and that no float appears in outputs.
The module imports no network, broker, provider, or market_data modules. A test or import inspection asserts this.
forbidden_changes: change PLAN_SKELETON.json or other planning artifacts
perform network, provider, clock, or broker I/O inside indicator code
use float arithmetic for indicator values
introduce hardcoded trading thresholds or profitability claims
run broad test suites or backtests
